statement: The node's three listener ports (REST API, admin WebSocket, cross-node transport WebSocket) form one coherent, fully-wired port model with a single derivation authority: (1) each port is a first-class config key with a schema property, env mapping, and default — no half-wired keys (node.wsPort today has no schema/env/default and is rejected by additionalProperties:false); (2) defaults form one base+offset family derived from restApiPort (REST = base, admin WS = base+1, transport WS = base+2) while each port remains individually overridable; (3) exactly one module owns port/address derivation and every consumer that today re-derives restPort+2 locally (entrypoint-runtime-options, node-address-resolution, cdc-integration-service-node-join, cdc-event-handler, connect-websocket-phase) consumes that authority instead; (4) startup validation rejects any configuration where two listeners resolve to the same port; (5) help text, Helm chart templates/values, and CLI defaults agree with runtime behavior — no advertised-but-unconsumed PORT env var, no hardcoded 8081 that contradicts the config model. Proven by deterministic red-on-revert tests (dt:prove) covering the derivation authority, the wired config keys, and the collision validation, plus a green test suite.
